# simplifyd_service_config (Resource)

A static config file mounted into a service's container.

`content` supports `${{VAR_NAME}}` interpolation, resolved at deploy time against the service's variables plus the `SERVICE`, `ENVIRONMENT`, and `PROJECT` system variables. In Terraform, escape those as `$${{VAR_NAME}}` so HCL does not try to interpolate them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "simplifyd_service_config" "app_config" {
  service    = simplifyd_service.api.slug
  name       = "app-config"
  mount_path = "/etc/storefront/config.yaml"

  # $${{...}} escapes HCL's own interpolation so the platform substitutes these
  # at deploy time. SERVICE, ENVIRONMENT and PROJECT are always available.
  content = <<-YAML
    environment: $${{ENVIRONMENT}}
    service: $${{SERVICE}}
    log_level: info
  YAML
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `content` (String) File contents.
- `mount_path` (String) Absolute path inside the container, e.g. `/etc/app/config.yaml`.
- `name` (String) Display name for the config.
- `service` (String) Slug of the service to mount the file into.

### Optional

- `env` (String) Environment slug. Defaults to the provider's `env`.
- `project` (String) Project slug. Defaults to the provider's `project`.
- `workspace` (String) Workspace slug. Defaults to the provider's `workspace`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<workspace>/<project>/<env>/<service>/<config>`.
- `slug` (String) Server-assigned slug.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Configs are identified by <workspace>/<project>/<env>/<service>/<config>.
terraform import simplifyd_service_config.app_config acme/storefront/production/api/app-config
```
